# Test Fixtures

| File | What it is | Used by |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `sample.pdf` | A hand-built, single-page PDF containing one line of text, "Visual Document Understanding Pipeline". 612 bytes. Valid according to the PDF header and trailer rules, and opens in any viewer. | The container smoke test, the tools (`benchmark.py`, `throughput.py`, `try_mcp.py`) and their tests, and the testing guide. |
| `sample.png` | A 2 by 2 pixel white PNG. 71 bytes. | The worker and document-check tests, the container smoke test, and the throughput tests, to cover the image path alongside the PDF path. |
| `eval/` | The evaluation set: three computer-drawn pages (an invoice in US dollars, a German invoice in euros with European number formatting, and a letter) whose correct reading is known exactly. | `tools/evaluate.py`, which scores the pipeline's readings against them. |

All of them were generated by short Python scripts rather than copied from
anywhere, so there are no licensing questions and they stay small.
`tools/make_eval_set.py` rebuilds `eval/`. The euro invoice needs a system font
with the euro sign (Arial on Windows and macOS, DejaVu Sans on Linux); the
script says so if it cannot find one.

**Do not send `sample.png` to the real worker.** It is blank, so a real reader
finds nothing on it, and the worker treats an empty reading as a failure worth
retrying: three paid readings, then `failed`. The demo worker never reads the
image, which is why the tests can use it.

## The evaluation set

Each document in `eval/` has up to three files:

| File | What it holds |
| :--- | :--- |
| `<name>.png` (or `.pdf`, `.jpg`, `.jpeg`) | The document itself. |
| `<name>.expected.md` | What a perfect reading returns. Required: a document without one is skipped. |
| `<name>.facts.json` | Optional. Short strings that must appear somewhere in the reading: amounts, names, dates. |

The three drawn pages are the easiest case there is. They prove the harness works
and catch regressions, but real quality work needs your own documents: scans,
photographs, and pages with several columns or long tables. To add one, put the
file in `eval/`, write its perfect reading by hand as `<name>.expected.md`, and,
if it has numbers or names that must come out exactly, list them in
`<name>.facts.json`. Section 13 of [testing-guide.md](../../testing-guide.md)
shows how to run the scores and compare two runs.

Do not commit anything confidential. These files are public once the repository
is.
